data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Consensus probability as n grows tends to 0: the dynamics whp gets trapped in a locally stable mixed configuration, because such obstructions are abundant. The obstruction structures are frozen colorings where every vertex has at least two of its three neighbors of its own color; equivalently the disagreeing edges form a subgraph of maximum degree 1 on each side. The simplest and dominant gadget is a pair of adjacent disagreeing-edge endpoints forming an isolated cross-edge between two internally monochromatic induced subtrees. Quantitative law: the expected number of such absorbing mixed configurations reachable from a random start grows exponentially in n (like c^n with c > 1 for a positive constant c), so the probability of consensus vanishes as n \u2192 \u221e.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If chains of flips can cascade through a frozen matching (a vertex temporarily in minority flipping and destabilizing the basin), the \u21920 verdict fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If simulations show consensus probability empirically near a constant strictly between 0 and 1 for large n, the \u21920 claim is falsified.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the frozen-at-time-zero set is actually o(n), the abundance mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Asynchronous updates fix vertices one at a time; once a vertex has a 2-to-1 local majority it is frozen, and freezing propagates outward from random initial seeds. Since a uniform random coloring already has a constant fraction of vertices in local majority-agreement, an \u03a9(n) set is frozen from step 0, and the dynamics merely prunes the boundary between color basins to a matching. With positive probability (bounded below, whp realized on random 3-regular graphs) both color classes retain \u03a9(n) vertices whose neighborhoods saturate into a stable matching, so no sequence of single-vertex majority updates can ever make the coloring unanimous: consensus probability is bounded away from 1 by an \u03a9(1) amount and in fact \u2192 0 as the number of independent frozen basins grows linearly in n.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
